### Contributing guidelines

- [X] I have read [CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md](https://github.com/nvim-mini/mini.nvim/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md)

### Module(s)

mini.ai

### Question

Hi,
A common workflow for me is being inside a large function (e.g. `main`) and wanting to edit a nearby `if`, `for`, or other brace-delimited block even though my cursor is not currently inside that block.
With vanilla Vim I typically need to move to the block first and then use something like `f{ciB`. I hoped mini.ai would help with this use case, but I have had trouble getting predictable behavior.
From my observations, when using brace textobjects, mini.ai sometimes selects the next `{...}` block, while at other times it selects the surrounding block that contains the cursor. In particular, one-line blocks seem to be treated differently from multi-line blocks, which can make the selection feel surprising. I may be misunderstanding the intended behavior, but I have found it difficult to build reliable muscle memory around it.
I also experimented with mappings such as `i}` → `in}` in operator-pending and visual mode. While this gets closer to what I want, it has drawbacks. Since these are mappings rather than true textobjects, if I pause after pressing `i`, Neovim eventually falls back to the default textobject behavior.
What I would really like is a way to define brace textobjects with a configurable search strategy on a per-textobject basis. For example, I would like a textobject that always selects the next `{...}` block after the cursor, even when the cursor is already inside another surrounding block.
Is there a recommended way to achieve this today, or would you consider supporting per-textobject search behavior in the future?
Thanks for your work on mini.ai.

comment_data.body:
> From my observations, when using brace textobjects, mini.ai sometimes selects the next `{...}` block, while at other times it selects the surrounding block that contains the cursor. In particular, one-line blocks seem to be treated differently from multi-line blocks, which can make the selection feel surprising. I may be misunderstanding the intended behavior, but I have found it difficult to build reliable muscle memory around it.

This is an intended behavior of `'cover_or_next'` search method and [is documented](https://github.com/nvim-mini/mini.nvim/blob/c594be5b095204e99473825ec2dee872e7409a4d/doc/mini-ai.txt#L542-L548).

> I also experimented with mappings such as `i}` → `in}` in operator-pending and visual mode. While this gets closer to what I want, it has drawbacks. Since these are mappings rather than true textobjects, if I pause after pressing `i`, Neovim eventually falls back to 

The only way to support this *is* via custom mappings. Both `a` and `i` in 'mini.ai' are custom mappings. So are `an` / `in` / `al` / `il`. If typing two character mapping is difficult due to timing, increasing `:h 'timeoutlen'` should help here.

the default textobject behavior.
> What I would really like is a way to define brace textobjects with a configurable search strategy on a per-textobject basis. For example, I would like a textobject that always selects the next `{...}` block after the cursor, even when the cursor is already inside another surrounding block.
> Is there a recommended way to achieve this today, or would you consider supporting per-textobject search behavior in the future?

The recommended solution here is to set `config.search_method = 'cover'` and explicitly use `next` / `last` variations to select a textobject in the specified direction.

reply_data.body:
> But just out of curiosity, how does vim by default identifies if it is inside {} and if not it gets to next {}.

It searches for a covering textobject first (potentially through a whole buffer) and then falls back to searching forward. This proved (for me) to be confusing when I expected it to select "next" textobject but in fact there was a very big covering textobject outside of the current window view. So reversing the order was the solution here until explicit `next` / `last` variants were implemented. The latter with default `config.search_method = 'cover'` is the suggested solution here.

> The solution you provided works but it would be better(I know that I am getting nitty-gritty) if you could provide options to disable to first search on current line, or different search_methods for different textobjects.

Explicitly defining search method via different mappings *is* the suggested solution here. If you want total flexibility, there is [`find_textobject()`](https://nvim-mini.org/mini.nvim/doc/mini-ai.html#miniai.find_textobject) function which can be used in custom mappings. But beware that there are plenty of small edge cases here. Consult how 'mini.ai' defines its own mappings to potentially avoid them.

> but for this I need ['{'] to be a miniAI textobject.

It is already a built-in textobject. Executing `=MiniAi.find_textobject('i', '{', {search_method = 'next'})` returns expected result. Also, make sure to not use `['{']` though, as this is a syntax error.

> Yes it is builtin textobject but it doesn't have vim like behaviour(it first searches for both on current line)

To force built-in behavior for some key sequence, the common approach is to map it to itself while using `remap = false`. I.e. analogous to `:xnoremap i{ i{`.
